Never After #2

Scarred

Emily McIntire, Ionel Ghiragosian (Translator)

3.84
228,538 ratings22,539 reviews
Rate this book
Într-o lume de basm întunecată, un prinț marcat de trecut încearcă să-și revendice tronul, dar se îndrăgostește de mireasa fratelui său. O poveste picantă despre trădare, dragoste și răzbunare care te va ține cu sufletul la gură!

EA NU-I APARȚINE LUI. ÎI APARȚINE COROANEI.

Prințul Tristan Faasa nu a fost niciodată în cărți pentru a ajunge pe tron. Acesta era destinul fratelui său, Michael. Același frate care este răspunzător pentru copilăria chinuită a lui Tristan, precum și pentru cicatricile care îi brăzdează chipul. Când tatăl celor doi frați moare, Michael se pregătește să urce pe tron, iar Tristan vrea să i-l fure. Liderul unei rebeliuni secrete, Tristan nu se va da în lături de la nimic pentru a pune capăt domniei fratelui său. Dar când lady Sarah Beatreaux, logodnica lui Michael, sosește la curte, Tristan se trezește în mijlocul unui alt gen de război. Genul care aduce cu sine întrebarea: oare care este mai importantă – coroana sau femeia care o poartă?

Sarah are un plan. Să se mărite cu regele și să pună capăt stirpei Faasa, chiar dacă asta înseamnă să se pună singură în primejdie. Nu se așteaptă însă la întâlnirea cu prințul cu cicatrici. Acesta este periculos. Interzis. Și unul dintre oamenii pe care a fost trimisă să-i ucidă. Însă linia dintre ură și pasiune nu a părut niciodată atât de subțire și, pe măsură ce secretele ies la lumină, Sarah nu mai știe în cine să se încreadă, prinsă între răzbunare și ticălosul de care nu ar fi trebuit niciodată să se îndrăgostească.

About the author

Emily McIntire

29 books30.2k followers
Emily McIntire is a #1 New York Times and #1 Sunday Times bestselling author of forbidden romance with flawed characters, slow burn tension, and a guaranteed happily ever after. Best known for reimagining legendary stories through a whole new lens, her books have sold millions of copies and have been translated into over a dozen languages, hitting bestseller lists around the world.

A stage IV breast cancer thriver, you can find Emily in Tennessee spending time with her family, feeding the crows, and serving her cats who think they run the house.

I was warned — I was told that this book would fall short, but I heed no mind. And now that I am disappointed, who am I to blame? Because as much as Hooked wasn't perfect, I enjoyed them, but Scarred feels like reading an entirely different work.

A thing that I love about McIntire's book is the disclaimer at the very beginning of the book because it helps the reader to lay the groundwork of the book's direction. So did I delve into the book with no expectation whatsoever since the author did say this will be a slow burn. However, as soon as I did, I realized that:
i) Era-themed is not my cup of tea if weren't done right — I think the reason why Hooked was an easy read was that it was set in a contemporary setting.
ii) Scarred is too slow for my liking — put an era-themed book with a deliberate build-up; better watch the paint dry anyway.
iii) The dialogue in this book is so calculated — it feels unnatural, consequently making some of the moments in the book sound just corny. I cannot take anything seriously, I'm sorry.

This also then makes me question if the only reason I enjoyed Hooked was because I was thrilled by the stamp of it being a Peterpan retelling, and everyone who knows me knows I am obsessed with Peterpan. Because not only this book has a predictable and boring storyline, the characters (even the H/h) are the blandest ones I've come to know.

The forbidden love sounds so promising and slow-burn supposed to serve as a wherein plot, methodically toward an explosive boiling point. Sadly, nothing was burning and there wasn't even tension between Sara and Tristan. I literally roamed through the book after the 30% mark because I couldn't find myself staying on a single page that long without falling asleep.

I was surprised to see that many had enjoyed this (like, why am I not on board with this). Maybe we were having a different prospect of what the book should be, I don't know; to each of their own. As for myself, I should've taken the warning seriously next time.

▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰

I've read and loved both Hooked and Wretched, but for some reason, this book was a let down of the worst king. The one that comes with boredom, to be precise.
I appreciated the "retelling" part (loved how the names were crafted around The Lion King's protagonists' or the quotes from the movie that were used, for example) and I also really liked the whole rebel king subplot, but in terms of romance, this book fell incredibly short for me, especially if we compare it to H and W.
I didn't feel the chemistry between the two main characters, not until when it started manifesting into actions and became obvious.
And I swear it has nothing to do with how much political intrigues the plot revolved around or the fact that the romance was a slow burn; slow burns are actually one of my favorite tropes, along with forbidden love, but I need something to work with in the space between "hi" and "let me come on your tits".
Tristan and Sara weren't bad, but their bond...I just didn't feel it in my belly and it gave me almost no emotion.
The smut was okay, but as tasteless as the rest of their relationship. I'm also incredibly tired of virgin heroines losing their V card and orgasming like they're porn stars on the set of their fourth film of the day. Lord have mercy on us mere mortals and on lazy clits everywhere.

Their characterization was slightly better.
I enjoyed Sara stubborness and how quickly she could put others in their place whenever they tried to wrong her, but she kind of lost a bit of her spark and her eges around the third act of the story. Tristan I liked a little better and, to be honest, if the book had been about him and the rebellion, I probably would have given this at least one more star.
That's to say, McIntire's writing never disappoints, no matter how dull the plot of her book is. I must admit, tho, that her dialogue weren't the best she's written in this. I missed a bit of her usual wit and the banter between Sara and Tristan was not my favorite by a long shot.
Not gonna lie, there were moments I thought I was wrong, that we were getting there, to the good part. But that was just what they were, unfortunately. Moments, too short and rare for salvation.

And, ugh...for some reason I started this 1) thinking the main characters were POC (because Lion Kind duh - and so the actual description threw me off), and 2) thinking this was set in modern times, but apparently it takes place in 1920s or something, but it was never really clear, and the writing certainly didn't help.
I also would like to start a petition to record the audiobook again with better narrators. Like I said in one of my reading updates, the narrator for Tristan sounded like a middle-aged history professor with coffee breath and patches on his tweed jacket's elbows. It was a major turn off and it made me cringe so much I managed to listen to only one chapter before I started fearing I'd develop a face paralysis and eventually turned to the e-book.
Sara's narrator was only slightly better, but not by much.

Anyway, I hate that I didn't like this, and I hate that I'll have to wait one more month to get my Never After fix, especially after this disastrous adventure.
But no worries, Madame McIntire, I still think you're the bestest and would love for this series to go on forever, even if I'll have to read about Pinocchio and Jiminy Cricket being in a dom/sub polyamorous relationship with Mangiafuoco.

2.75 stars

“You could burn down the entire kingdom until it’s nothing but charred rubble, and I would crawl over the embers with glee, so long as I could worship at your feet.”


Another dark fantasy retelling with tropes like forbidden romance, slow burn, and dark romance with historical and royal vibes. Honestly, this book has some of the most amazing tropes, but I still didn't like it the way I thought I would. I had high expectations after reading the synopsis, and it was enjoyable and a very quick read, but it didn't have the spark I was looking for—especially since this series is practically about stories where the villain gets the girl. Tristan and Sara's witty banter and the delicious spicy scenes in this book made up for all of it. I must admit they were very hot together.

“I’m your future queen,” I whisper. “Maybe you should show some respect.”
His eyes spark at this, his hand reaching out and touching one of the spiral curls that’s fallen from my hairpin. He winds it around his finger, the corner of his mouth lifting into a mocking grin.
“Well then, I’ll be sure to work on my curtsy.”


Tristan Fassa, “The Scarred Prince,” the rebel king of Gloria Terra, is nothing but a vile, crude, and dangerous man. Because of his bad reputation and tattooed body, everyone is afraid of him. Tristan's past was devastating, and I hated how some people treated him so badly just because he was a little different. His past is the reason he is who he is now. Now, all he craves is revenge. He was annoying because he couldn't stop talking about his hard-on every other second and because of his severe god complex. Though he does have a very useful and smart mouth.

“If something happens, know that I will find you in every lifetime, Sara Beatreaux. You are mine, and not even death can keep you from me.”

“She’s a fucking vision. The kind that should hang in galleries and be revered by the masses. The perfect type of art. Mine.”

“I am nothing, if I’m not yours.”

“I can’t feel anything but loving you.”


Sara Beatreaux was a disappointment. I thought she would be a badass and witty woman, not some damsel in distress, because she said, and I quote, “I’ve never been one with ideas of grandeur, thinking some white knight will ride in on his steed and save me like some helpless damsel in distress. There may be distress, but I’m no helpless damsel.” She is adventurous and cunning when planning to get revenge for her father's death. She is also good at putting up a façade of an innocent and naive girl who wants nothing but to marry the king.

All Tristan and Sara ever wanted was revenge and nothing else. The moment Tristan met Sara, he knew that she wasn't what she seemed. They became enemies who were ready to kill each other, with daggers at each other's throats. It all started with lust, obsession, and insta-love. Tristan and Sara both saw something in each other that no one else did. They literally went from "killing each other" to "dying for each other." The whole idea of burning down the world just to save each other and ruling together was actually good—if a little too much and obsessive.

“The truth is, I am yours. Wholly. Inexplicably. Painfully. Unconditionally.” He moves my hand until the dagger presses against his throat.
“And if you need to sacrifice my soul so you’re able to live with yours, then do it.”


The beginning really kept me intrigued, and I thought, yes, this might be my favorite of this series. I don't know when or where I got bored; it felt like so much was happening, but also nothing was happening. The plot was intriguing, but the mystery was really predictable, which left me underwhelmed when all the secrets and truths were unraveling. I'm not disappointed because I actually enjoyed most of the parts, so it's a win for me, I guess. The writing was easy and simple to read, and the pacing was normal considering it was a slow-burn romance. But after reading two of Emily's books, I now know that her stories kind of follow the same pattern of insta-love, lust, predictable plot twists, and anticlimactic endings. The first half will make you want more and more, but the second half will leave you with nothing—just too much drama and rushed endings. I liked how the characters in this book were portrayed much better compared to Hooked. They are still not very likable and a bit messed up.

The ending was okay. It wasn't what I expected; it felt rushed and a little anticlimactic, as I already said. I would have liked it more if some things weren't skipped just to make this book a few pages shorter.

This series is not for me, so it's time to part ways with Emily McIntire before it's too late.

3.5 Little Doe Stars ⭐️

Everybody loves a bad boy and when that bad boy happens to be a disgustingly sexy SCARRED prince with black hair it is totally fair to say expectations are pretty high and I’m not ashamed to say I had skyscraper-level expectations for this. Unfortunately, this didn’t even peak at a two-story condo.

This is nothing "Lion King". The description was actually right! It is an embraced reimagining of Hamlet and if anything it would be a prequel to The Lion King, except in this one Mufasa is a cruel vindictive dick who beats on his brother and murdered his father. So said brother wants to get him back where it hurts most…stealing his crown and kingdom.

The main problem with this book was the writing! It was incredibly messy, like imagine on the level of a high school paper that you’d written the night before the deadline and had to come up with 5000 words at 2 o’clock in the morning. The general descriptions, the sentences and how things were laid out at times made no sense. I get EXTREMELY frustrated at books when I am forced to re-read sentences. If it happens once or twice I can overlook it; BUT in this the entire first 20% of the book, I was in a perpetual state of confused-mess. This made it very difficult to get into the story as I was constantly rereading stuff and needing to go back and try and put together in my mind what was fuck was going on because it wasn’t clearly communicated.

The pace and plotline of this were choppy and chaotic. I am not sure if it just felt this was because of the mediocre writing but things would happen off-page and then as the reader you are just thrown into the mix again - I had to page back a few times to make sure I WASN'T SKIPPING CHAPTERS by mistake. We are just shown the repercussions of these events, which is bad plot design in my opinion!

Next... in the BLURB and Author's note at the start "It is a fractured fairy tale: NOT FANTASY" - Genres on Goodreads - FANTASY???? Like what are you?? Honestly, this read like a fantasy, but there wasn't enough world-building to feel that this WAS FANTASY! There is this made-up kingdom that is close to FRANCE???? And they have guns and automobiles BUT they also use swords!!! I had no idea what time period this was in or what world.

The one thing I liked though is Tristan and Sara, but I didn't love them! I think I have been spoilt recently in ACTUAL fantasy where the characters have so much depth to their characterisation and the relationships are complex and convoluted. These are just two people who are horny and slightly psychotic that their attraction borders on obsessive possession... Again, like Hooked, this felt 100 pages too short to explain how quickly these characters say "I love you". BUT I don't think I would have been able to survive another 100pg of this!

As I alluded to in my mini review - I liked this more than Hooked only because I connected slightly more with the characters and agreed with the motivations they had - Also the way Tristan was with Simon was adorable! BUT I preferred the writing in Hooked...

So right now I am left underwhelmed, unsatisfied and disappointed that this was not amazing! I wanted the trend to be true that if you didn't fully love Hooked, you would like this - but sadly this one didn't do it for me either.

Would I still recommend this?
Yes - it's not terrible and I can see why people love this for what it is. It's a good way to pass the time - the smut was also fine, nothing scary and dark... just a few candle wax drips to excite you!

⊱------------------------------⊰

I didn’t love it, some parts were good though and I enjoyed this more than Hooked (but only barely), but I also did not vibe with this book… 😭😭😭😭😭

“You thirst for power?” he rasps, his palm ghosting across my collarbone before wrapping around my throat. “I can fill you with it until you scream.”

Scarred is a deliciously dark and seductive 1910's royal romance of a scorchingly hot forbidden love between the King's bride-to-be and the Prince, the King's enigmatic younger brother.

If you're looking for a couple that paint themselves in every shade of morally grey with traces of villainy seeping through them, do not go far.

Meet Lady Sara Beatraux and the dangerous and wicked Prince, Tristan Faasa—known as the Scarred Prince. The story takes place in the 1910's but in an entirely fictional Kingdom.


— Forbidden Romance
— Court Intrigue
— Slowburn Enemies-to-lovers
— Extremely morally grey/villain love interest who is a hot dark-haired tattooed prince with an impressive artistic talent.
— Delicious spice
— Dark ambience
— Complex characters


Driven by a desire of vengeance, Lady Sara seeks to avenge the death of a loved one—the easiest way to ensure her plans come to fruition is by heading into the Lion's den and offer herself as a bride to King Michael Faasa III of Gloria Terra.

“I’m no one’s queen. I’m just the one who will burn the crown.”

As soon as Michael's bride-to-be sets foot in the Saxum Kingdom, Tristan knew behind that soft innocent exterior is a cunning temptress who thrists for power. But she is to be family right? And so Tristan plans to give his future sister-in-law a very warm welcome.

“I should kill you for making me feel this way.”
“So kill me, then,” she whispers.
“Death would be a gift. I’d rather see you suffer.”

Tristan and Sara are swept by a blinding passion and a dangerous attraction for one another that they can't help but dance their forbidden waltz.

“And if I were to take you?”
“Then I’m yours for the taking.”

Like, damn... you could feel the passion and chemistry between Tristan and Sara scorching right through the pages. The secret liaisons, the lingering hungry stares, hiding in dark corners. I thoroughly enjoyed every scene they were together. Their scenes were swoon-worthy, exciting, and nerve-wrecking.

And just like Sara, I could not help but be drawn to Tristan's dark allure and cruelty.

The court intrigue and drama was perfectly balanced with the romance, you truly felt there were so many things at stake and of course, there are quite a few plot-twists that catch you off guard.

The author promised a morally grey borderline villainous couple and she truly delivered! They committed devious and cruel actions but that is how their own world shaped them to be.

“I’d like to draw you. Just like this, with your face kissing the stars... I think it’s the most beautiful thing I’ve ever seen.”

The author's writing style was intricate and quite immserive that I could not put the book down.

Honestly, this was such a fun and an immersive read. Definitely one of the best dark royal romance books.

Trigger Warnings: violence, death, substance abuse, torture, attempted se*ual assault, su*cide.

This was really bad... I feel like everyone else thought this was amazing, and I truly don't understand. The pacing in this was way off, the plot is boring and convoluted, the backstory is non-existent, the characters are SO unlikable, and the whole thing comes off as a bit confused. I finished it, but not before contemplating a DNF about 10 different times.

First, the plot is... strange. This is set in the 1910s, but think kingdom. From the very beginning nothing in the writing stood out to me as specific imagery pointing to the 1910s, so I think the setting is sort of a moot point. Even the backstory/world building is super unclear. It's a kingdom, there appears to be some sort of court system with dukes, duchesses, etc., but that's all we get. I don't even really understand the state of the kingdom, what the economy is like, or anything else. I'll go ahead and stop here and say maybe I have too high of exceptions, but I wish at least some of this was explained as it all very much ties into the characters and their motivations.

Now, onto the characters. We have Lady Sara Beatreaux, our h. She is moving into the castle, as she is to be married to King Michael. Although, that's not her only goal. She's planning on advenging her father who was killed by the king. The king's little brother, Tristan, is our H. He's the reclusive sociopathic one. He often lurks in the shadows, is extremely anti-social, and has tons of tattoos. He bears a horrible facial scar, but of course, he's still gorgeous. Tristan has his own motivations that are later revealed, but I'll just say he hates his brother and seemingly the whole idea of their royal family. He holds a lot of rage based on past trauma. These two, while working through their own plans, find themselves entangled together due to what is essentially unwanted attraction? I guess that's the best way I can frame it. The development of their relationship is very slow burn.

Both characters are honestly terrible, and a huge reason why I hated this. I couldn't root, or even enjoy, either of them. Sara for example - I feel like she's a bit all over the place. She has moments of "softness". Caring for others, she explains how much she hates death after losing her father, etc. But at the same time has 0 regard for human life or anyone who stands in her way. It's very odd watching her flip from being quite caring to then justifying someone's death as a causality to her plans. It doesn't make her complex, it makes her seem psychotic. Her character is honestly dull and a bit annoying. As a side note on the backstory here, but I still have 0 idea why Sara was the woman chosen to marry Michael. We are told her father was a duke, and it sounds like her part of the kingdom/the kingdom as a whole is super poor and not doing well? But idk, nothing is ever fully explained.

Tristan, on the other hand, certainly isn't dull but he's psychotic and even harder to like than Sara. He's not just a morally grey, villain character. He is completely horrible, has no problem killing others or doing anything he can to get what he wants. I know this is a dark romance, but Tristan is truly irredeemable. Honestly, this isn't even that dark. It's just two terrible people, with nothing good or decent about them. Tristan's "love" for Sara is better described as a strange obsession.

Their relationship together is oddly developed, and way too slow. I felt like I was reading forever to finally find the spicy bits. Plus, disliking the characters made me disinterested in the romance and their development together. They both are sort of drawn to each other because they are equally selfish and messed up... That's their only connection, this idea they are both "dark" people...

Now, back to the plot. A main theme throughout the book are these rebels who hate the king and want to overthrow him. But again, the motivations aren't even that clear. Why exactly does Michael suck? Is the kingdom in that bad of shape? I think the story is alluding to people being super poor, but it's never truly shown or explained. Just that there's a group of "others" (hyenas) who live on the outskirts of society and hate the king. Like ok, but what about the rest of the kingdom? Again, none of this is well explained to the reader so it's difficult to care. With how slow and long the romance took to develop (honestly ugh so boring), I would expect the other storylines to be well explained. But this feels like it can't really stand up on its own. Then the ending was so rushed and awful. Sara and Tristan's plan was successful based on basically luck. None of their planning or strategy was made known to the reader. Everything just sort of exploded and worked out for them in the end. I don't know if this book was supposed to be a romance, a political coupe fiction, or something else entirely.

To be honest, I am really surprised so many people love this. I can usually tell when a book is not for me, but in this case I think the story is poorly done. Even if someone reads this purely for romance and smut - and ignores the plot + issues with the backstory/world building - you're still having to wait until at least 70% of the way through for the romance and smut to actually take place (and when it does it's like a couple of times)... I didn't love the first book in this Never After series, so I don't plan on continuing with the series or author.

This is NOT a Lion King retelling in the sense that IT IS but the author would very much like to not be sued by the behemoth that is Disney, so please don’t call it that.

😅 Sorry, but there were too many elements present for me to call this anything but a VERY loose retelling.

Scar ✔️
Elephant Graveyard ✔️
Hyenas ✔️
Timon & Pumbaa… err I mean Timothy & Paul ✔️✔️

If you want to take it even further, this is the full breakdown of the characters…

* Sara B.- Sarabi
* Scarred Prince (Tristan)- Scar
* Michael Faasa - Mufasa
* Simon- Simba
* Kara- Kiara
* Sheina- Shenzi
* Edward- Ed
* Timothy- Timon
* Paul- Pumbaa 
* Raf- Rafiki
* Zander- Zazu

As you can see, the gang’s all here…

A Lion King retelling certainly wasn’t on my 2024 bingo card, but I didn’t hate it. I enjoyed it a lot more than Hooked at the very least. Scar was definitely evil and a little too into torture for my taste, but something about the more medieval setting allowed me to look past those traits for the most part. He also didn’t kidnap her like Hook did, so there’s that.

I did like Tristan and Sara together but I am really not a fan of the way this author writes intimate scenes. There’s dirty talk and then there’s nasty talk and I think this author writes the latter. I’m sure some people are into that, but it’s not for me. It also felt on the verge of being nonconsensual. I would have liked at least one scene where she said no and he listened to know that he would not have forced her. He was bothered when someone else tried to force her but it seemed more because “she was his to touch” than because he was against forcing himself on a woman in general.

My expectations were honestly pretty low, but I would recommend this to the right person. I have to say that I do think this series is pretty overhyped though. If you love it, I’m happy for you, but I think it’s not for everyone. I’ll stick to morally gray men and let you keep your villains. 😅✌🏻
______________________________________________

Is this a Lion King retelling? 😅 Surely not, but I can’t think of any other scarred villain princes…

Giving myself permission to DNF this if it’s anything like Hooked. I was not a fan but decided to give the series one more shot.

Prince Tristan Faasa was never destined for the throne that was always his brother Michael. The same brother is responsible for both Tristain's tormented childhood and the scar on his face. When their father dies, Michael is set to assume the throne yet Tristain is set to steal it. Tristan is the leader of a secret rebellion and will use this to stop his brother's reign. But when Michael's new betrothed Lady Sara Beatreaux arrives, Tristain finds himself in the middle of a new kind of war. The kind that begs the question of what's more important the crown or the woman about to wear it. She doesn't belong to him, she belongs to the crown. Sara has one plan. Marry the king and eradicate the Faasa line, even with the risk of her peril. She never expected to meet the Scarred Prince, he's dangerously handsome. Now the line between hatred and passion has never looked so thin. As secrets come to light, Sara grows unsure of who she can trust. Will Sara remain torn between vengeance and the villain she was never supposed to love?

All my reviews have the possibility of spoilers, be warned!

So far this is the best book in this series. It has everything you would want: amazing characters, entertaining dynamics, and a brilliantly thought-out plot line. I refuse to accept any criticism from this book. I love how Tristan is a scarred man, I love my men with scars. I instantly knew he was going to be loveable. When it came to torture scenes we were lucky and fed. We got it off both Tristan and Sara. I didn't know who did it better at that point.

There are so many quotes from this book that will simply make you swoon. And if you didn't I would be beyond shocked.

"I prefer you this way. On your knees, chest heaving, and face flushed while you stare up at your betters."

"I see. You thirst for power?" he rasps, his pale fingers ghosting across my collarbone before wrapping around my throat. "I can fill you with it until you scream."

"You'd make a stunning portrait."
"What?"
"I'd like to draw you, just like this, with your face kissing the stars I think it's the most beautiful thing I've ever seen."
"I'm saying you could drive a man insane. Make him raze the world just to see you smile."

"I'm going to kiss you now," I tell her.
"Why?" she whispers.
"Because, ma petite menteuse, the thought of not kissing you makes me want to die." Our lips collide, and with just one touch one single moment I know I'll never let her go.

This scene was my favourite in this book. God the way Tristan spoke to Sara my heart was full. I was rooting for them in the beginning and seeing this scene had me kicking my feet and giggling. I cannot see another couple in this series beating Sara and Tristan they were so good together. Tristan quite literally would sacrifice himself and everything he had for Sara, it was so beautifully done.

"Are you going to kill me, little doe? I do not wish to see you fail. Even at this."

"Ma petite menteuse, the world is full of lies. The truth is, I am yours. Wholly. Inexplicably. Painfully. Unconditionally." He moves my hand until the dagger presses against his throat. "And if you need to sacrifice my soul so you're able to live with yours, then do it."

"You think I wished for you? I would scourge the earth if I thought it would erase you from my brain. The problem is, Sara, there is no erasing you. And now you're part of me. One that I can't snuff out, no matter how much I may try. And I'm part of you too. Even if you hate that it's so." But he drops to his knees instead, his arms splaying wide at his sides. "I am nothing if I'm not yours. So do it. Kill me, Sara. Put me out of this constant purgatory of needing you without having you. I will die happily if it's what will bring you peace."

I am in love with both Tristan and Sara you cannot force me to choose between them, nope.

I push up on my elbows and stare down at what he drew. It's a heart. Not the kind that you see kids draw or the type that you would expect in paintings that depict love. This one is of the organ, blood dripping off its edges and running through the muscle. A thick chain wraps around its centre and coils beneath it, a padlock on the end. I squint my eyes and look closer, realizing there's writing on the lock. Tristan's Property.

"If something happens, know that I will find you in every lifetime, Sara Beatreaux. You are mine, and not even death can keep you from me."

"Tell my brother that if he doesn't give me Sara, I will burn this entire city, this entire country to the ground until he has nothing left to rule."

"What were you thinking, burning everything down like this?"
I glance at the Saxum castle, my home for the last twenty-six years and my family's legacy for the last three centuries, and shrug. "They wouldn't give you back."

I cannot wait to see what other childhood stories Emily is going to modernise!

I’m not really into writing a huge review so this’ll be short, sorry💔


I’m not really into this genre too much and in all honesty I didn’t like the first book of the series (Hooked) because I couldn’t accept some of the topics (Stockholm Syndrome the most important of them all), but I wanted to give the author + the series a second chance and this was way better.
This book was good, but I’m still not really into dark romance (I’m trying though😅). It was a really fast read and really entertaining. Comparing it to Hooked (which are totally different) this is a masterpiece, at least Sara was a strong character, otherwise I would’ve kms. I liked all the references of The Lion King that the author wrote and the plot was good. Also, all my favorite tropes were on the book so that’s a win.

The characters were good, my favorite of course was Sara B.. She’s kind and very determined and I appreciated that because Wendy (Hooked FMC) was the complete opposite and I hated it. I also liked Tristan and his rebellion, but I didn’t like that he referred to himself like he was a God (I’m not religious but I hate men with huge egos). Michael is a piece of sh*t, that’s all I have to say. Simon was also my favorite character, a little boy who’s adorable, playing with a toy sword and looking up to Tristan as a role model.

Things I didn’t like:
-Why is Tristan 24/7 turned on?
-Sara’s tattoo (the property thing iykyk).
-Some chapters were meh.
-Not too much romance/spice.
And I don’t remember much more😅.


Thanks to my beautiful girl Hoda for buddy reading this book with me, I love you so much and cannot wait for the next one🤎🤍♥️.

a fantasy inspired by lion king? inspired by scar? SCARRRRR !! I love lion king so so much ,so of course I had to read this and I WAS NOT DISAPPOINTED.

The story revolves around Sara Beatreaux , the daughter of a duke sent to the king as a candidate for marriage . Sara seeks to avenge her dead father and overthrow and rid the world of the Faasa family. She is warned to stay away from the kings scarred brother who dark rumor's follow but she cannot help but be swept by the beautiful and cunning prince into a scorching and passionate romance

"i should kill you for making me feel this way"

This book was addicting and hottttt . I feel Emily really captured and executed the lion king resemblance. Tristan (scar in this case) was a dark and complicated character , he really was messy and cruel and I really appreciated how he didn't have some abrupt change in his behavior after Sara came along , he was every bit the anti-hero while still earning my love . Sara could have been developed a bit better in my opinion , she didn't really have much character , what did she like ? who exactly was she ? but it was good enough and she certainly wasnt one of those annoying Mary sue characters , neither was she great at everything she did . The scenes between the two were absolutely steamy , with lingering stares , exciting situations and burning passion . I'm usually not one for smut but I actually didn't mind it being here . I do wish the physical attraction was focused on a little less however .For a book meant to be set back in 1910 it didn't really feel that way much , the book read more like a contemporary romance with bits of a fantasy world mix which kept the pace going .The plot with the court dealings and world building was done really well . I usually find myself unsatisfied and wanting more after a standalone and though I could take more of these two I find the book was ended suitably and we weren't left hanging .

"I'd like to draw you", I rephrase, moving in closer,my fingers dancing across her skin."just like this, with your face kissing the stars...I think its the most beautiful thing I've ever seen."

if your moral compass is slight skewed , if your a bit on the insane side ( my kinda people) then I urge you to read the book .If you liked the cruel prince i think ud want to check this out too. its not gonna be everyone's kinda thing so be sure to check TW's before reading the book.
